newsitem.title: USA: Chantal had anticipated higher 1996 sales.
newsitem.headline: Chantal had anticipated higher 1996 sales.

text.p: Chantal Pharmaceutical Corp said while its fiscal 1996 sales increased, they fell short of its expectations and that much of the costs incurred during the year had been made in anticipation of higher sales.

It said those expenditures included product components, advertising, promotional materials and the launch of an extensive nationwide marketing campaign with appearances on national and regional talk shows.
The company's fiscal 1996 revenues rose to $13.2 million from $7.2 million, but fell sharply in the 1997 first quarter to $1.9 million from $5.2 million in the year-ago period.
The company said its business was hurt by negative publicity and questions surrounding its accounting practices.
"Fiscal 1996 was the most difficult and challenging year in the 14-year history of (the company)," Chantal Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Chantal Burnison said in a statement.

"Although the company's marketing plan was delayed as a result of the negative publicity during 1996, based on the company's current marketing program, we believe that we are back on track toward profitability," she said.
